title: Cold open on the best moment
why: Opening on the most intense moment from later in the video promises that it's coming.
formula: [5–10 seconds of the peak moment.] Cut. "[Time marker] earlier…"
check: Does the cold open make sense without context, and does the video really reach that moment?

hooks.say: 'It's not going to hold.' … Okay. Three weeks earlier, this was a pile of boards.
hooks.frame: The shelf wobbling as you put the last book on it.
hooks.next: Introduce the project, the deadline and the one part you weren't sure would work.

hooks.say: This is the moment the client saw the final cut. To get here, I threw away the first two.
hooks.frame: The client's face lit by the laptop, silent.
hooks.next: Say in one sentence what was wrong with version one, then promise what changed.

hooks.say: We were forty minutes in when she said the thing that made us scrap the episode plan.
hooks.frame: The guest mid-sentence, the host completely still.
hooks.next: Cut to the start of the conversation and tell viewers that moment is coming.

hooks.say: That's the sound of a two-thousand-dollar camera hitting the floor. Let me explain how we got here.
hooks.frame: A black screen and the crash, then the camera on the floor.
hooks.next: Rewind to the morning of the shoot and lay out what was supposed to happen.

hooks.say: The timeline froze, the export failed, and we had ninety minutes until the deadline.
hooks.frame: The laptop screen with an error message.
hooks.next: Put the clock on screen and introduce the project.

hooks.say: At the end of this video, I hand a coffee to a judge who has tasted thousands of them.
hooks.frame: The cup sliding across the counter.
hooks.next: Jump back to day one of practice and show your first bad pour.

hooks.say: This is the last step of a walk I've done every week for a year. The first one is where I nearly quit.
hooks.frame: Shoes stopping at the top of a staircase.
hooks.next: Go back to week one, say why you started and what changed.

hooks.say: I'm about to read you the most honest feedback I've ever had. It took me a month to open it.
hooks.frame: The message full screen, your face in a corner circle.
hooks.next: Say who sent it and why it mattered, then promise the changes you made.

title: Show the result, then promise the method
why: Proof first, then a clear promise of what viewers will be able to do by the end.
formula: This is [the result]. By the end of this video, you'll [be able to do it yourself].
check: Is the promise specific enough that viewers can tell whether you delivered?

hooks.say: This is a ten-minute video I edited in one evening. By the end of this, you'll have the exact order I do it in.
hooks.frame: The finished video playing on a screen, then your face.
hooks.next: Show the five steps as a roadmap on screen, then start step one.

hooks.say: This shelf cost me thirty dollars in wood. I'll show you every cut, including the one I got wrong.
hooks.frame: The finished shelf, with a slow push in.
hooks.next: List the tools on screen, show the sketch and start measuring.

hooks.say: That's latte art from a home machine. By the end, you'll know the three things the machine doesn't do for you.
hooks.frame: The finished heart, from above.
hooks.next: Introduce the three things as chapters and start with milk temperature.

hooks.say: This one page plans my whole week in ten minutes. We're going to build it together from a blank page.
hooks.frame: The finished spread, then a fresh page.
hooks.next: Show the four sections you'll draw and start with the first.

hooks.say: This audio was recorded in a bedroom. By the end of this, yours will sound like this, with no new gear.
hooks.frame: Your face at a microphone, levels steady.
hooks.next: Play the before clip, then lay out the three fixes.

hooks.say: These are my last ten Reels. They all use the same structure, and I'm going to give it to you.
hooks.frame: A grid of the ten Reels full screen, you in a corner circle.
hooks.next: Name the four parts of the structure on screen and start with part one.

hooks.say: This dress started as two old curtains. You'll be able to make one by the end of this video, even as a beginner.
hooks.frame: The curtains on the left, the finished dress on the right.
hooks.next: Show the materials and pattern pieces, then cut the first piece.

hooks.say: This phone footage was graded in two minutes. I'll show you the exact sliders.
hooks.frame: The graded shot, freezing as the label lands.
hooks.next: Open the editing app and name the four sliders before touching them.

title: Ask the question the video answers
why: A real question, asked early, gives the whole video a reason to exist.
formula: Why does [something people notice but can't explain]? I spent [time] finding out.
check: Is it a question your viewers have actually wondered about?

hooks.say: Why do some badly lit videos get millions of views while beautiful ones die? I went through two hundred of them to find out.
hooks.frame: A rough phone clip on the left, a polished one on the right.
hooks.next: Explain how you picked the videos and what you measured.

hooks.say: Why does café coffee taste better than mine when I use the same beans? I asked three baristas.
hooks.frame: Your face, then two cups side by side on a counter.
hooks.next: Introduce the baristas and the test you'll run with them.

hooks.say: Why does every handmade table wobble a little? It turns out it's not the legs.
hooks.frame: A hand pressing on a table corner as it rocks.
hooks.next: Show three likely causes and say which one you'll test first.

hooks.say: Why can I remember a song from ten years ago but not what I studied yesterday? The answer changed how I take notes.
hooks.frame: Headphones on, then a notebook opening.
hooks.next: Explain the idea behind it in plain words and show the note layout you'll build.

hooks.say: Why are two-person podcasts easier to listen to than solo ones? We recorded the same episode both ways.
hooks.frame: Two hosts at their microphones, side by side.
hooks.next: Play ten seconds of each version and say what you'll compare.

hooks.say: Why do some streets feel safe at night and others don't, with the same street lights? I walked both for a week.
hooks.frame: Walking down a street at dusk.
hooks.next: Show the two streets on a simple map and what you'll be looking for.

hooks.say: Why does your video look fine on your phone and awful on a laptop? It's one setting.
hooks.text: Fine on phone, awful on laptop
hooks.frame: The same clip on a phone and a laptop.
hooks.next: Show the setting, then explain why it matters before changing it.

hooks.say: Why do beginners break so many needles in their first week? I broke six to find out.
hooks.frame: A close-up of the needle punching through fabric.
hooks.next: Line up the six causes as a countdown.

title: Set the challenge and the clock
why: A goal, a limit and a deadline give viewers a reason to stay for the outcome.
formula: I have [time or budget] to [goal]. If I [fail], [consequence].
check: Is the clock or budget on screen whenever it matters?

hooks.say: I have one hour to edit a full YouTube video with only free tools. If I go over, I post it unfinished.
hooks.frame: A timer starting on screen beside you.
hooks.next: Show how much raw footage you have and the tools you're allowed.

hooks.say: Twenty dollars, one weekend, and I need a bookshelf strong enough to hold all of these.
hooks.frame: A stack of books next to a pile of scrap wood.
hooks.next: Break down the budget and sketch the design.

hooks.say: I'm making a café-quality latte at home with no espresso machine, and a barista is judging it.
hooks.frame: An empty counter and your friend with their arms crossed.
hooks.next: Introduce the judge, the score sheet and your three attempts.

hooks.say: Can I film, edit and post a video every day for a week while working full time? Day one starts now.
hooks.frame: Walking out of the office, phone up.
hooks.next: Put the daily schedule on screen and the rule if you miss a day.

hooks.say: I have to explain this whole topic in ten minutes, or the next guest gets my slot.
hooks.frame: A timer on the desk between the microphones.
hooks.next: State the rules and start the timer.

hooks.say: I'm walking every street in my neighbourhood in one day. There are forty-one of them.
hooks.frame: Shoes on the first step of the route.
hooks.next: Show the route on a map and say when you'll stop if you can't finish.

hooks.say: I'm going to sew a jacket in a day, and I've never made a sleeve.
hooks.frame: Pattern pieces laid out, the needle ready.
hooks.next: Show the pattern, set the deadline and admit the hardest part.

hooks.say: One phone, no lights, and I have to make this product look like an ad by sunset.
hooks.frame: A product on a table, phone in hand, the sun getting low.
hooks.next: Show what you have to work with and the reference you're trying to match.

title: Test it so they don't have to
why: Viewers love skipping the trial and error. A fair test with a clear winner pays that off.
formula: I tried [N options] for [time]. [One surprising result].
check: Did every option get the same conditions?

hooks.say: I tested five AI editing tools on the same raw clip. One of them cut my best line.
hooks.frame: Two versions of the same clip side by side.
hooks.next: Explain the rules of the test and what counts as a win.

hooks.say: I bought the four most recommended microphones under a hundred dollars. The cheapest one surprised me.
hooks.frame: Your face at the first microphone, with a counter in the corner.
hooks.next: Play the same sentence on each mic before naming any of them.

hooks.say: I tried every cold brew method I could find. One takes twelve hours and loses to one that takes five minutes.
hooks.frame: Jars of cold brew lined up on the counter.
hooks.next: List the methods and explain the taste test.

hooks.say: I used three planners for a month each. I'm keeping one and binning two.
hooks.frame: Three notebooks stacked, one being opened.
hooks.next: Show what you'll measure: tasks done, missed days and time spent planning.

hooks.say: Same scene, four phones, no editing. Can you tell which one is the cheapest?
hooks.frame: The same street shot side by side.
hooks.next: Explain how you filmed each one and ask viewers to guess.

hooks.say: I sanded this board with five different sanders. The best finish came from the slowest one.
hooks.frame: The sander on the first test strip.
hooks.next: Explain how you'll judge the finish and start with the cheapest sander.

hooks.say: I tried four ways of learning lines for a video. One of them let me record in a single take.
hooks.frame: You reading off a phone, then not needing it.
hooks.next: List the four methods on screen and start with the one most people use.

hooks.say: We asked five guests the same question. Their answers were the opposite of what I expected.
hooks.frame: Quick cuts between guests at the microphone.
hooks.next: Put the question on screen and play the first answer.

title: Lead with your thesis
why: A clear position in the first ten seconds tells viewers exactly what you're going to prove.
formula: Everyone says [belief]. After [your experience], I think [your view], and here's the evidence.
check: Will you show evidence, not just opinion?

hooks.say: Everyone says you have to niche down. I grew fastest when I made whatever I was curious about, and I'll show you the numbers.
hooks.frame: Your subscriber graph full screen, you in a corner circle.
hooks.next: Walk through your channel history in three phases.

hooks.say: The part of good coffee worth spending on isn't the machine. It's the grinder, and I can prove it with one cup.
hooks.frame: A grinder next to a cheap machine.
hooks.next: Set up the blind taste test.

hooks.say: Productivity systems don't fail because you're lazy. They fail because they're built for someone with no kids, no commute and no bad days.
hooks.frame: Your face, then a perfect planner page with coffee spilled on it.
hooks.next: Show the three assumptions most systems make.

hooks.say: Good editing is mostly deleting. In this video I'll cut a ten-minute talk to three, and you'll like it more.
hooks.frame: A long timeline shrinking.
hooks.next: Play the first minute raw so viewers have something to compare with.

hooks.say: Hand tools are faster than power tools for most small jobs. I timed it.
hooks.frame: A hand saw on one side, a power tool on the other.
hooks.next: Explain the timing rules and the three jobs.

hooks.say: Walking is a better creative habit than journaling, and I've done both every day for a year.
hooks.frame: Shoes on the pavement, a closed notebook on a bench.
hooks.next: Show your two logs side by side and how you scored the ideas.

hooks.say: Most podcast advice is about gear. What actually made our show better was a list of bad questions.
hooks.frame: A notepad of crossed-out questions on the desk.
hooks.next: Read the first bad question and explain why it fails.

hooks.say: Beginners should skip the beginner projects. Make the thing you actually want to wear.
hooks.frame: A pile of half-finished tote bags.
hooks.next: Show the project you'll make and the two skills it teaches.

title: Open with a confession
why: Admitting a mistake builds trust quickly and sets up the lesson.
formula: For [time], I [did the wrong thing]. This is what I wish I'd known.
check: Is the confession real, and does the video deliver the fix?

hooks.say: For two years I edited every video like a trailer, and my audience hated it. This is what I changed.
hooks.frame: Fast flashes of an old edit, then your face, still.
hooks.next: Show one old video and one new one, and name the three changes.

hooks.say: I undercharged every client for my first three years. This is the price list I use now, line by line.
hooks.frame: The old invoice full screen, you in a corner circle.
hooks.next: Explain how you worked out the new numbers before showing them.

hooks.say: I ran a café for a year and never once tasted our espresso the way a customer would.
hooks.text: Never tasted it like a customer
hooks.frame: Your face, then espresso pouring, close.
hooks.next: Tell the moment you realized, and what you tasted.

hooks.say: I've started this video four times because the topic embarrasses me. So I'll just say it: I can't read a map.
hooks.frame: Four quick restarts of the same opening.
hooks.next: Admit how it has affected you and what you're going to try.

hooks.say: We nearly cancelled this podcast after episode ten. Nobody was listening, including my co-host.
hooks.frame: A host at the microphone glancing at a phone.
hooks.next: Show the download numbers and what you changed in episode eleven.

hooks.say: I've sold eighty tables, and I've never told anyone I can't cut a straight line by hand.
hooks.frame: A wobbly pencil line on the wood.
hooks.next: Show the jig you use to cheat, then build it.

hooks.say: I said yes to every brand deal for six months. These are the three I regret.
hooks.frame: Your face with a counter in the corner.
hooks.next: Explain why you said yes, then start with the worst one.

hooks.say: My first ten videos got zero views because I never watched them back. Let's watch one together.
hooks.frame: The old video playing on a phone screen.
hooks.next: Pause on the first mistake and explain it.

title: Preview the mistakes
why: A numbered list of mistakes promises useful fixes and a clear end point.
formula: [N] mistakes I see in [thing]. [Tease the worst one].
check: Is each mistake something viewers can check in their own work today?

hooks.say: These are the five editing mistakes I see in almost every beginner's first video. Number four is the one I still make.
hooks.frame: Your face with a 1/5 counter in the corner.
hooks.next: Go straight into mistake one with an example on screen.

hooks.say: I reviewed thirty channels that asked for feedback. The same three mistakes came up in almost all of them.
hooks.frame: A channel page full screen, you in a corner circle.
hooks.next: Show how you reviewed them, then reveal mistake one.

hooks.say: Four milk-steaming mistakes, and the reason your foam disappears in thirty seconds.
hooks.frame: Foam collapsing in a cup.
hooks.next: Steam one jug the wrong way, then name mistake one.

hooks.say: Six things people get wrong when they start woodworking. I made every one of them.
hooks.frame: The sander working along the edge of a board.
hooks.next: Show mistake one on a scrap piece.

hooks.say: Three interview mistakes that make guests give short answers, and what to ask instead.
hooks.frame: A guest giving a one-word answer.
hooks.next: Play a short answer, then the better question and its answer.

hooks.say: Five note-taking mistakes students make, ranked by how much time they waste.
hooks.frame: Pages of copied-out notes being flipped.
hooks.next: Start with the smallest time waster and build up.

hooks.say: The four camera settings I see wrong most often in phone videos. You can fix all of them before your next shoot.
hooks.frame: A thumb on the camera dial.
hooks.next: Open the settings and fix setting one on camera.

hooks.say: Three mistakes that make beginner sewing look homemade, in a bad way. None of them are about skill.
hooks.frame: A puckered seam next to a flat one.
hooks.next: Name mistake one and show the fix on the same seam.
